title: AHO-InDNN: An Efficient Hybrid Optimization Algorithm for Fraud Detection in E-Commerce Using Improved Deep Neural Network
authors: D. R., J.; Sheela, A.; Raj, A. J.; Priyadarshini, Y.; Basha, S. M.
tldr: Proposes AHO-InDNN, a hybrid optimization algorithm combining Artificial Hummingbird Optimization and Hunger Games Search with an improved deep neural network for binary fraud detection in e-commerce transactions.
problem_and_motivation: E-commerce fraud causes massive financial losses and transaction volume makes manual detection impractical. Existing ML-based fraud detection suffers from class imbalance and suboptimal hyperparameter tuning.
approach: Proposed cascaded hybrid optimization (AHO + HGS) with Lévy flight and Roulette wheel selection to balance exploration and exploitation.
Improved DNN with cross-entropy loss and L2 regularization for fraud classification.
Preprocessing: encoding categorical features, standard scaling, SMOTE for class imbalance handling.
Evaluation on two e-commerce transaction datasets with 16 features each, 44% fraud ratio.
Compared against 8 baseline algorithms: SVM, RF, DNN, PSO-DNN, GWO-DNN, BOA-DNN, WOA-DNN, AHA-DNN.
findings: num: AHO-InDNN achieved 98.8% accuracy, 98.7% precision, 98.5% recall, 98.6% F1-score, 0.01 FPR.
num: AHO-InDNN outperformed the best baseline (AHA-DNN) by 1.8% in accuracy and 2.5% in F1-score.
Hybrid optimization (AHO+HGS) outperformed individual metaheuristics (AHA, PSO, GWO) for DNN tuning.
Cascaded design reduced computational cost compared to parallel hybrid approaches.
Lévy flight escape mechanism prevented premature convergence in local optima.

key_equations.equation: AHO-InDNN = AHA + HGS + Lévy flight + Roulette wheel + Improved DNN
key_equations.explanation: Cascaded hybrid optimization combining AHA exploration and HGS exploitation with flight mechanisms.

key_equations.equation: Cross-entropy loss: L = -Σ y log(ŷ) + λ/2 ||w||²
key_equations.explanation: Loss function minimizing prediction error with L2 regularization to prevent overfitting.

definitions.definition: Artificial Hummingbird Optimization — metaheuristic inspired by hummingbird foraging behavior for global search.
Hunger Games Search — metaheuristic inspired by hunger-driven animal behavior for local exploitation.
Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique — generates synthetic samples for the minority class to address imbalance.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides a novel hybrid optimization algorithm (AHO-InDNN) that demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on e-commerce fraud detection. The cascaded hybrid approach (AHA exploration + HGS exploitation with Lévy flight escape) offers a computational efficiently alternative to parallel hybrids. The approach is directly applicable to fraud detection modules in PFMS.
directly_justifies: Hybrid metaheuristic optimization improves DNN hyperparameter tuning for fraud detection.
Cascaded hybrid design balances computational cost with optimization quality.
SMOTE is effective for handling class imbalance in transaction fraud datasets.
limits: Evaluated on only two datasets with fixed 44% fraud ratio — generalization uncertain. [acknowledged]
No explainability mechanism for fraud detection decisions. [unacknowledged]
Computational complexity comparison against baselines is limited. [unacknowledged]
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was performed. Domains 8.A (fraud detection) and 14.A (ML approaches) were flagged as highly relevant because the paper proposes a novel ML algorithm specifically for fraud detection. Domain 14.B was flagged as low relevance because no XAI mechanism is provided. Domains 1-7, 9-13 were rejected as the paper focuses purely on algorithmic fraud detection without addressing user profiling, budgeting, savings, or other PFMS aspects.

limitations: Tested on only two datasets; real-world generalization not established. [acknowledged]
